cross_product_finding: Two distinct cross-product observations here. (1) Feature gating: auditing is gated on an 'Enterprise Support Plan' - this is a Capella-native gating axis (a purchased support/service tier) that is a genuine parallel to, but NOT the same as, server/'s requiresEdition (Enterprise Edition vs Community Edition). I minted requiresSupportPlan rather than reusing requiresEdition, since a support plan is a commercial/contractual tier orthogonal to product edition, and the batch background confirms Capella has no EE/CE concept at all. (2) Reference reuse: for the actual catalog of auditable events, this Capella page does NOT define its own event list - it defers entirely to server/'s Audit Event Reference for Enterprise Server 7.2 and 7.6 ('The Audit Event Reference... for Couchbase Enterprise Server Version 7.2/7.6'). So while Capella's ACCESS-CONTROL model (org/project roles) is a different shape from server/'s RBAC, its AUDIT EVENT CATALOG is literally the server/ catalog, tied to specific server/ version numbers. This means version:server-7.2 / version:server-7.6-style concepts legitimately belong in relations that describe server/ content Capella docs point to, even though Capella's own pages shouldn't be tagged with those versions directly. I minted server:audit-event-reference-7.2/7.6 rather than reusing version:server-7.2/7.6 directly, to keep the 'this is server/'s reference, just linked from a cloud/ page' distinction explicit. The internal-user list for audit exemptions (@eventing, @cbq-engine, @ns_server, @index, @projector, @goxdcr, @fts, @cbas) is also identical to server/'s internal system users, further reinforcing that Capella's audit subsystem is the underlying server/ auditing facility exposed almost unchanged, in contrast to its access-control layer which IS Capella-specific.
